subject: history
title: The Decolonisation Chain in Southeast Asia

slides.heading: The Decolonisation Chain in Southeast Asia
bullets: How independence spread from territory to territory after the Second World War: the Philippines wins independence in 1946, Indonesia is recognised in 1949, Malaya follows in 1957, and Singapore wins internal self-government in 1959 - each win raising nationalist pressure in the next territory
slides.notes: Welcome everyone in and say: today we follow one chain across Southeast Asia, where each independence made the next one harder to refuse.

slides.heading: What we will learn
bullets: Explain how independence in one territory raised nationalist pressure in the next, stage by stage from 1946 to 1959
Show the chain in order: Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959
slides.notes: Read the two goals aloud and tell the class: by the end you will be able to run the whole chain in order and say what carried it from one territory to the next.

slides.heading: Four territories, four dates - coincidence, or a chain?
bullets: The Philippines, Indonesia, Malaya and Singapore all had different leaders, parties and negotiations
Yet their breakthroughs came one after another between 1946 and 1959 - what connected them?
slides.notes: Ask the class: if each territory acted entirely on its own, why did the breakthroughs bunch together in just thirteen years? Take two or three answers, then say: hold them, because the animation shows a pressure bar, not four separate stories.

slides.heading: Pressure is carried from neighbour to neighbour
bullets: An independence next door is proof it can be done: campaigners point to it, colonial control looks weaker, and nationalist pressure rises past the threshold
Colonial control falls stage by stage as each territory wins, so the next campaign starts from a stronger position
slides.notes: Stress the deciding idea: the territories were linked by a chain - the example was carried on, and pressure in each territory started higher because of the win before it.

slides.heading: Philippines, 1946: pressure crosses the line
bullets: After the Second World War, nationalist pressure in the Philippines rises past the threshold line
The United States grants independence in 1946, the colonial control bar falls, and a transmission arrow carries the example on to the neighbours
slides.notes: Play scene 1 and point to the pressure bar crossing the threshold: the first link of the chain is forged in 1946.

slides.heading: Indonesia, 1949: the example raises pressure
bullets: Indonesian nationalists point to the Philippine example: if a neighbour could win independence, so could they
Pressure rises, and after the struggle the Netherlands recognises Indonesian independence in 1949
slides.notes: Play scene 2 and follow the transmission arrow in: the example from 1946 lands as extra pressure, and recognition follows in 1949.

slides.heading: Malaya, 1957: pressure rises, control falls
bullets: In Malaya the pressure bar rises again, helped by two neighbours now independent, while the British control bar keeps falling
Malaya wins independence in 1957, the third link of the chain
slides.notes: Play scene 3 and compare the two bars: pressure up, control down - the same mechanism, one stage further along.

slides.heading: Singapore, 1959: the chain reaches home
bullets: The chain reaches Singapore, where campaigners have watched three neighbours win in thirteen years
Singapore wins internal self-government in 1959 - not full independence, but the chain has reached home
slides.notes: Play scene 4 and note the careful wording: 1959 brings internal self-government, the stage the animation claims, with the example of three neighbours behind it.

slides.heading: Worked example: running the whole chain
bullets: Philippines 1946: pressure crosses the threshold and independence is granted; Indonesia recognised 1949: the example raises pressure next door
Malaya 1957 and Singapore internal self-government 1959: pressure rises and control falls at every stage, carried on by the transmission arrows
slides.notes: Work it slowly: Step 1, Philippines 1946. Step 2, Indonesia recognised 1949. Step 3, Malaya 1957. Step 4, Singapore internal self-government 1959. At each step ask: what carried the pressure up - the local campaign alone, or the neighbour who had just won?

slides.heading: Your turn: run the chain in order
bullets: In pairs: starting from the Philippines in 1946, state each stage of the chain in order and what rises or falls at that stage
Then swap and check: did your partner show the example being carried on, or four separate stories?
slides.notes: Give pairs three minutes. Listen for the full chain in order, then take two pairs answers: Philippines 1946, Indonesia recognised 1949, Malaya 1957, Singapore internal self-government 1959, with pressure rising and control falling at each stage.

slides.heading: Exit ticket: prove it before you leave
bullets: Your exit ticket asks you to correct a student who says each colony won independence entirely on its own
Name the four stages in order and the carried example between them to earn full credit
slides.notes: Point to the exit ticket and remind the class: the strongest answers run the chain in order and name what each win did to pressure in the next territory.
